articles.chapeau: An extra $1,300 hidden right at the start of 'GTA 6'? Don't mind if we do.

Grand Theft Auto VI has only been out for a day , but people are already sharing tips.
One early hidden feature — and a nice way to quickly build those cash reserves — comes courtesy of a liquor store and a talking parrot.
UK streamer Millzaa shared a mini walkthrough of how to find the money in GTA 6 on TikTok and X , where it's been viewed over a million times.
"There's a parrot that leads you to a secret money stash at the start of GTA 6 ," he says in the video. "Talk to your neighbor Shirley and she'll send you to the liquor store for some rum..."
Millzaa explains that once you've bought and delivered the rum for Shirley you can return to Three Sheets Liquor (when you're in the store earlier, the owner tells a bunch of animals in a back room to be quiet. Don't try to enter this room by walking behind the counter (the owner will not like this). If you jump the fence round the side you'll find some criminals you need to fight off — and when you do, you'll discover a talking red parrot in a cage. The parrot mentions cash and a generator, next to which you'll find a grate in the wall.

articles.txt:
Cyberleek, the account previously linked to major Grand Theft Auto 6 gameplay leaks, is again claiming to distribute a pre-release build of the game. In a statement posted on its website on November 19, the account said it possessed a “full November 2026 build” for Xbox and was releasing the files by torrent.
Cyberleek said the build totals 209 gigabytes but that it had withheld the main executable—the file needed to launch the game. The account claimed it would release that final component only if the market capitalization of its $CYBERLEEK meme coin reaches $15 million. It also said the build was for Xbox, not PC, and predicted that users would get it running through emulation. Those claims have not been independently verified.
Reports say files purporting to be part of the build are circulating online, but it remains unclear whether they are authentic or complete. Cyberleek said it would seek a PlayStation 5 build as a fallback if the Xbox version could not be made to work, though it suggested that would probably not be necessary.
The latest announcement follows a similar threat in October, when Cyberleek said it would release a GTA 6 build if its cryptocurrency reached a $30 million market capitalization. The account instead published a series of escalating leaks, including nude footage of Lucia, one of the game’s two playable characters. The coin later fell in value, and the account went quiet.
It is not known whether the person or people behind the latest claims are the same individuals responsible for the earlier leaks. Cyberleek appears to have previously sold or otherwise profited from the meme coin, while Rockstar Games and its parent company, Take-Two Interactive, have not publicly identified those responsible for obtaining or distributing the allegedly stolen material.

'GTA 6' on Xbox Series S: How well it actually runs
articles.chapeau: Here's the verdict.
articles.txt:
Reading through Reddit, there is no shortage of concerns about how well Xbox Series S will or won’t run the game. As the release neared, fans seemed confident that Rockstar Games would ensure the game was playable, but opinions varied widely on what graphical sacrifices would be required for it to run, including reduced crowd density and scaled-back visuals.
How much time did I spend sweating the idea of crowd density? Too much. Did I ever think about it or care about it until Redditors said it’ll likely be less on the Series S? Not at all.
And yet, while it filled me with regret for not buying a PS5 last Black Friday before the price hikes arrived, it did not stop me from buying GTA 6 on Xbox Series S, debating whether or not to resist the pull off the New Zealand timezone trick to play it early, and preparing to explore Leonida.
And now, having played GTA 6 for a few hours, I can tell you everything you need to know about how it runs and how it feels.
I won’t keep you waiting: GTA 6 runs smooth as butter on Xbox Series S. There were no stutters, no lag or other slowdowns that pulled me out of the gameplay.
During a prologue that introduced me to protagonists Jason and Lucia, I quickly experienced a variety of locations in daytime and nighttime, as well as rainy weather. After that, I was able to play around Leonida and check out all the basic things that might catch your attention as you play: how the weather looks, flying down the road in a car through busy streets, random tasks around Jason's home.
In addition to moving quickly through various areas, I also took a moment to slow down. I watched a sunset by the water, went for a swim surrounded by fish, and observed how the environment affected Jason. Nothing slowed down, glitched out, or made me think anything other than I was playing a AAA game.
What I can’t tell you right now is how much better GTA 6 is or isn’t on PS5 or any of the higher-end consoles. We’re in the process of comparing the Xbox Series S version to the PS5 Pro version as we speak.
Rockstar has explicitly said the game will run best on PS5 consoles, with faster load times and technology that may improve resolution. The PS5 Pro version will also include ray tracing, making the lighting even more eye-catching. But both games will still be locked at 30 frames per second, according to Rockstar. The game developer did not say if any other sacrifices had to be made to get it to run on the Xbox Series S.
Regardless, what I can tell you is there is a good game waiting for you to play on Xbox Series S. If you don’t have the funds to upgrade your console, do not let comparison be the thief of joy.
GTA 6 is a generational moment in gaming and a cultural moment much larger than any game launch I’ve ever seen. The game is fun, the music is a vibe, and the world is immersive without feeling like a chore. I can't imagine waiting to play this if they have the means to do so right now.

articles.t: GTA 6: Should You Choose Saved Cash Or Say Nothing In "Buck Me"
articles.chapeau: There's one right choice to make here.
articles.txt:
By Ben Brosofsky Published Nov 19, 2026, 10:27 PM EST Ben Brosofsky has been writing for Screen Rant since 2022 and editing since 2024. He graduated from Vanderbilt University with a Bachelor's in Cinema & Media Arts. Writing serves as a much-needed distraction from tackling a backlog of Steam games that will never be surmounted. Sign in to your ScreenRant account "Buck Me" is one of the shortest missions in Grand Theft Auto 6 , but unlike plenty of more robust ones, it does present Jason with an intimidating choice . With his financial future — and Lucia's — potentially on the line, making the right decision can seem like an objective of the utmost importance.
GTA 6 doesn't offer much time to choose, as the prompt to select between saying nothing or mentioning Jason's saved cash comes and goes on a quick timer. If you've paused the game in search of an answer, though, here's everything you need to know about the choice.
After Jason picks up Lucia from prison and spends his first night with her, he'll get a new mission to take care of the next day, courtesy of Donnie. "Clean Up After Donnie" will take Jason north to locate a missing package, and as he heads up that way, Lucia might go ahead and ask him to join her at the bank when it's convenient for him.
Finish Donnie's objective, as this will ultimately take Jason back in the direction of the bank anyway. After wrapping that up, head to the nearby bank, go inside, and talk to the teller. She'll direct Jason to the manager, and once those two begin to converse, Lucia will appear.
When speaking to the bank manager, it quickly becomes clear that Jason and Lucia aren't in a great position to set up a bank account or take out any loans. Jason does have one asset, however: his saved cash, which he keeps under a floorboard in his bedroom.
When asked about the potential to deposit money, the option to mention Jason's saved cash is on a timer. You can also actively choose to say nothing, but if you wait too long to mention the cash, Jason will do this by default.
Faced with the timed choice, you should choose Saved Cash . The first chapter of GTA 6 features plenty of opportunities to impress Lucia by giving Jason a responsible attitude, and this is one of them. Choosing Saved Cash will immediately boost their relationship , while choosing to say nothing will do the opposite.
You can check out a full profile of ScreenRant 's guides for GTA 6 here .
Unfortunately, the relationship perk is the only active effect of this choice. Due to their credit scores, Jason and Lucia are ultimately unable to open a bank account at this time, even if the cash is mentioned. Regardless of which selection is made, they'll be pushed to use the BuckMe app, which Jason can deposit money into via ATMs and use for various payments. Money can also be transferred from the standard BuckMe account into a Family Savings profile, providing a more long-term savings goal.
If you do make the mistake of choosing to say nothing (or you simply run out of time), it's not the end of the world. Grand Theft Auto 6 features plenty of opportunities to improve the relationship between Jason and Lucia. This is a particularly easy one to take advantage of, but making up the deficit shouldn't be much of a challenge.

articles.t: Cyberleek GTA 6 Xbox Build: 209 GB, No Executable
articles.chapeau: Cyberleek says it released a 209 GB GTA 6 Xbox build. The executable is missing and a PC port is unconfirmed. Here is what reports confirm.
articles.txt:
Image: Rockstar Games An anonymous leaker or group calling itself Cyberleek says it has put a GTA 6 Xbox build on torrent networks, and the claim surfaced on November 20, 2026, one day after the game reached players. Coverage from Notebookcheck, PC Gamer, Nacionale, Eurogamer.net, Wolf’s Gaming Blog and VideoCardz.com describes a roughly 209 GB download labeled “XBOX BUILD 1.0.2.1 (NOV 2026).” The files reportedly leave out the main executable, so nobody can launch them as a finished game today.
That gap is the whole story. The release arrives as Grand Theft Auto VI rolls out worldwide and as PC players ask the obvious question: could an Xbox build bring a playable PC port within reach? Cyberleek says yes, and says it could happen fast. Nothing in the coverage confirms that the build is genuine, complete, or runnable on a PC.
This analysis separates what outlets have reported from what Cyberleek has merely claimed. It also looks at why the timing matters, what the incentives behind the release look like, how the leak compares with Rockstar’s earlier security problems, and what readers should do (and avoid doing) while the story develops. Anything not backed by the reporting stays general here, and unconfirmed claims are labeled as such.

Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.
Cyberleek is the name the anonymous leaker or group uses in the coverage. The reports agree on the basic shape of the drop. The files are described as an Xbox build, not a PC build, and they circulated through BitTorrent-style distribution. The label attached to the package reads “XBOX BUILD 1.0.2.1 (NOV 2026),” which points to a build made in the same month as the retail launch.
Reports put the download at approximately 209 GB. That is large enough to look like a real game package, though size alone proves nothing. A torrent of that weight could hold shipping assets, a mix of old and new data, or padding. Outlets have not verified the contents file by file, and no outlet in this coverage says it ran the build.
Coverage also attributes a line to Cyberleek, unconfirmed in its exact wording: “It is an Xbox build this time, not a PC build.” The phrase “this time” implies earlier releases, and it also implies that the group knows PC users are the audience that cares most. The reporting does not identify who Cyberleek is, how the group obtained the files, or whether it has any link to Rockstar’s staff or partners.
The naming of the game itself is inconsistent across the material. Outlets write GTA 6, GTA VI and Grand Theft Auto VI interchangeably, and this article follows suit. None of that affects the substance, but it explains why search traffic splits across several spellings today.
The table below sorts the claims by how well the coverage supports them. “Reported” means outlets describe it, not that they verified it. “Unconfirmed” means the claim comes from Cyberleek or from rumor and no outlet has tested it.
The pattern is easy to read. The facts that can be observed from outside (a torrent exists, it has a size and a label, it lacks an executable) are reported. Everything that would make the leak useful to a PC player is unconfirmed. That is a thin foundation for the “realistic PC port” framing that headlines have used.
A modern game package holds two broad kinds of material. Assets such as models, textures, audio and level data make up most of the bytes. The executable and its supporting code decide how those assets load, render and behave. Without the executable, a 209 GB pile of assets is closer to a very large archive than a game.
That is why reporting stresses the absence. Cyberleek has withheld the one file that would let anyone test the build, and the group has tied its release to conditions that benefit the group. Whether the executable exists in Cyberleek’s hands is not established. Whether it would run even if it did is a separate, equally open question.
There is a second reason the gap matters. Assets alone let researchers study content, such as map layouts, audio and art direction. They do not by themselves let anyone play. For Rockstar, the damage from an asset leak is mostly spoilers and reputational noise. The damage from a runnable build is different in kind, because it creates a way to play without paying.

articles.t: GTA 6 Has A Surprising Late Game Cameo That Knocked Me On My Ass
articles.chapeau: I'm shocked people are already seeing this moment as it is hidden near the very end of the story
articles.txt:
Across social media and YouTube, a massive spoiler from the final chapter of Grand Theft Auto 6 has been spreading online. It is a cameo by a past character that has people going wild. Some fans who have sped through the game’s story are rushing to be the first to share it online. Others don’t believe it’s even real. I’m here to confirm that, yes, the wild cameo you saw is real, and it made me scream.
This is your last warning. The next paragraphs are going to completely reveal the spoiler. If you are a massive GTA nerd and/or love surprises, stop reading now and close this article. Seriously, you’ll thank me later. For those who don’t care about spoilers, GTA lore, or who were never planning to play the game, let’s dive into one of the biggest surprises hidden within the massive world of GTA 6. Last chance to turn away. See you on the other side.
Near the tail end of GTA 6 ‘s big, epic crime story, Jason and Lucia begin working with Giorgio, a wealthy shipping magnate. He’s been working with some cartels and Eastern European criminals and has been letting them use his ships to smuggle cocaine across the ocean. It’s been working out pretty well for a while, but by the time Jason and Lucia show up, the Coast Guard has seized all the drugs from a recent shipment. He has a plan to rob the Coast Guard, get his coke back, and make everyone happy before they come to his big penthouse and kill him. But then, just as his big heist is coming together, a higher-up from the Balkan criminal family he’s been working with shows up to put a bullet in his brain.
And the person sent to Vice City is none other than Grand Theft Auto IV protagonist Niko Bellic. Yup. As shared online by many players already , a much older Niko shows up in two cutscenes to threaten Giorgio and then to collect the drugs once the heist works out. Here are those cutscenes:
I will admit that before he showed up, when I heard Giorgio yell out, “Daddy’s back bitches!” I chuckled to myself and thought, “Oh nice, a reference to the opening line of GTA IV. Cute.” I had no idea that would be followed up by the reveal of fucking Niko Bellic. I might have let out a scream and paused the game in pure shock and amazement.
We’ve not heard much about Niko since the ending of GTA IV. So seeing him back in the flesh, with grey hair, was great. And I love that Rockstar got back the original voice actor, Michael Hollick. And yes, that’s why in the credits of GTA 6 posted online by Rockstar, he is simply labeled “The Hitman.”
I can’t wait for more GTA fans and nerds to discover this moment and share their reactions. I’ll have more to share about the cameo and how it came about soon from my interview with Rockstar Games head of production Rob Nelson. But for now, let’s just enjoy the fact that Niko is back, baby.

articles.t: 'GTA 6' inspires DoorDash, UberEats, Grubhub discount codes
articles.chapeau: Food delivery orders have reportedly spiked around the game's launch.
articles.txt:
Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) was finally released into the wild on Nov. 19, unveiling the beloved video game franchise's first title in 13 years. The highly anticipated game even inspired eager fans to take time off work in favor of immersing themselves in GTA 6 , reveling in everything from crashing planes to home renovation in-game.
Yet while our virtual avatars engage in miscellaneous violent crimes, our physical bodies still require sustenance. Food delivery apps such as Uber Eats , DoorDash , and Grubhub have thus jumped on the GTA 6 hype, offering discount codes to those too locked in to their marathon gaming session to cook.
DoorDash's GTA 6 discounts are the most limited in terms of food options, offering $6 off Cheesecake Factory orders of $20 or more. Customers just need to enter the discount code CAKEGTA6 when placing their DoorDash order, with the offer only available on Nov. 19.
The company is also offering $15 off orders of $20 or more from Wendy's with codes given out on the Wendy's Twitch stream until 9 p.m. ET / 6 p.m. PT (check the scrolling bar at the top of the screen). However, these DoorDash codes are limited to the first 100 customers , and only valid for 30 minutes after they're released.
Uber Eats' discount code ONAMISSION will save users $10 off an order of $20 or more, and isn't restricted to a specific restaurant. Uber Eats has indicated this code is specifically for GTA 6 's launch day , so if you're interested you should redeem it sooner rather than later.
Grubhub's discount code OUTOFOFFICE offered $10 off orders over $10, and was active from 9 a.m. ET / 6 a.m. PT on GTA 6 launch day. Unfortunately, it was limited to the first 1,000 customers , with some people reporting that they were unable to use the code within minutes of the promotion being posted. Less than an hour and a half later, Grubhub confirmed that its GTA 6 -inspired discount code had been exhausted .
Food delivery apps have apparently received an influx of orders surrounding GTA 6 's launch. The New York Times reports that DoorDash's energy drink sales spiked by over 20 percent on Wednesday, when many Grand Theft Auto fans stayed up for the game's midnight launch. DoorDash's Wednesday night sales were reportedly up by double digits in multiple U.S. states, while UberEats' overnight sales increased by 30 percent in Miami (the inspiration behind GTA 6 's Vice City).
The next few days may be busy for food delivery workers, with gamers expected to spend hours exploring GTA 6 . As such, remember to be patient and tip well. No doubt they'd rather be playing as well.

articles.t: Controversial GTA 6 Easter Egg Will Annoy Millions of Gamers
articles.chapeau: A physical game joins NFT jokes as relics of the past included in GTA 6
articles.txt:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is now out everywhere, and players are discovering just how much this game is filled to the brim with an overwhelming amount of things to do. In the game’s opening hours, you’ll land a place on the water, steal a car from a police impound, get into a car chase, and more. There are a million little things to do, like playing video games inside GTA 6 itself.
Early in the game, Cal, a friend of co-protagonist Jason, spends an afternoon gaming with his buddy. Ironically, he does something that IRL players can’t do with GTA 6 itself: bring a physical game disc with him.
As GTA 6 ’s nearly 20 million players (at the time of this writing) know, GTA 6 is digital-only . “Physical” copies simply contain a digital download code in a box. As such, you can’t bring your copy of GTA 6 to a friend’s house to show them the game like you could with previous GTA games, or like how Cal introduces Jason to Tenebrae Lux , a very artsy game that spoofs Jonathan Blow’s The Witness . (Jason’s not impressed; he’d rather go kill zombies.)
The two then have a party-filled night together that ends with them drunkenly fighting over who gets to sleep in the bed, which then cuts to the both of them sharing the bed in their undies. It’s a surprisingly wholesome sequence that includes Jason opening up about the strains in his relationship with Lucia on the eve of her getting released from prison. The moments of genuine friendship between Cal and Jason contrast well to the rest of GTA 6 , which is all about, ya know, stealing drugs from rednecks, evading death-by-gator, running away from cops, and all other kinds of wild shenanigans.
Would you look at that — a physical game case on the coffee table. Image: Rockstar Games via Polygon Trading games, bringing a game disc to a hang sesh with the boys, introducing a new game to a friend by popping your copy into their console — for years, sharing games was easy because they were all on discs or other physical formats. When I reviewed the Gears of War remaster last year (with a digital copy), it reminded me how I first played the original game by trading my copy of Assassin’s Creed with a friend for his copy of Gears . Fast-forward to this year, and I’m playing Pokémon Pokopia by borrowing my partner’s copy. (OK, maybe I stole it from her Switch 2 case, who can say.)
PlayStation once famously demonstrated how to share used games in a 2013 video intended as a dig toward the always-online Xbox One. That joke has aged like milk in the wake of Sony’s announcement that it will cease manufacturing physical discs for PlayStation games in January 2028. Sony’s news hit just a short time after Rockstar Games announced its own digital-only plans for GTA 6 back in June.
Tenebrae Lux, a video game inside GTA 6. Image: Rockstar Games via Polygon Sony’s move prompted a wave of angry commenters spamming every PlayStation promotional video and blog post with disdain ever since. Some PlayStation owners tried to wrangle together a “no disc, no buy” blackout campaign where they wouldn’t use PSN, make purchases at the PlayStation Store, or basically engage with their PlayStation console in any way. That blackout had no effect on Sony . In fact, Sony’s digital game sales have continued to grow since the announcement.
The outrage over the decline of physical games clearly hasn’t had an impact on Rockstar’s GTA 6 either. It broke preorder records , despite there being no real need to preorder a copy — they’re all digital, so Sony and Microsoft won’t be running out. This isn’t 2009, when you had to preorder a physical copy of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 to make sure you could pwn some newbz day one. (And snag a sleek poster in the process.)
Though we can’t say with certainty yet, it seems likely GTA 6 will end up as 2026’s top-selling game, in spite of the uproar around its lack of a disc version. Yet none of the eleventy billion people who buy it will be able to share it with their buds in the way that Cal shared a disc version of Tenebrae Lux with Jason.

articles.t: It's Not 'Car Mechanic Simulator,' But GTA 6 Is Leaning Harder Into Vehicle Repair Than Before - Jalopnik
articles.chapeau: While you won't be wrenching on engine components yourself, "Grand Theft Auto 6" does feature a more complex vehicle maintenance system than previous games.
articles.txt:
Rockstar Games Add Jalopnik on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover More so than any of its predecessors, "Grand Theft Auto 6" leans heavily into realism. You can't just carry your entire arsenal on you anymore — instead, you must rely on a few guns on your person and a stash in your trunk . Building off that simulated realism, the game now puts a greater emphasis on the exciting world of vehicle maintenance directly into the gameplay. There will be times when you have to get your car repaired, repainted, or refueled. Who knows — maybe "Grand Theft Auto 7" will go one step further by including a mission called "Doing Taxes."
To be fair to "Grand Theft Auto 6," it does remember that it is an action/adventure game and not the next coming of "Car Mechanic Simulator." For instance, stops to get your car fixed are generally pretty brief. That way, you can get right back to running heists and stealing a car that looks a lot like a Pontiac Trans Am out of a police impound lot .
Still, the game does feature four different ways to get your car fixed: Pay 'N' Spray shops, mod shops, gas stations, and a guy named Joey who can be called upon to do repairs. Gas stations are limited in the repairs they can do and are more expensive than other repair shops — there's that realism again. For more extensive repairs, you'll need to stop at one of the other shops or call Joey.
Rockstar Games Missions can be pretty rough on your vehicles, especially when you're trying to get away from the cops. Your car can get engine damage or cosmetic damage, and fixing it can be important to the gameplay. One of the early missions, "Just a Scratch," will actually make you take your vehicle into Coastal Auto Care to get fixed. That's where you meet Joey.
Throughout the game, there is an engine condition indicator that goes from green to orange to red. It ends off at red with an "X" in the middle, indicating that the engine is dead. Green indicates the engine is in good shape, orange means there is moderate damage, and red indicates critical damage. An engine that is not in good shape can affect how the car performs, which is not something you want to deal with as your wanted level increases.
And don't forget to fuel up , as each car has a working fuel gauge. But don't worry, because you won't have to stop for gas too often; apparently "Grand Theft Auto 6" cars get pretty great gas mileage. EVs are also a part of the universe, which means you'll have to stop for a charge every so often if you grab one.
Rockstar Games The cars in "Grand Theft Auto 6" are not indestructible, but they can keep running even after getting pretty banged up. So, why bother to fix body damage? You don't want the NPCs to point and laugh at your car, do you? Even if you aren't worried about the opinions of Vice City pedestrians, the condition of your car's body can affect gameplay as well. Want to sell that hot car that you just stole? Well, just like in real life, damage to the body of the car can affect how much it sells for.
Then there's the matter of getting away from the cops after stealing a car. They will often have the car's description, including its color. There are even Flock-like cameras in GTA 6 that can track your movements . Repainting it another color, even when the body is in good shape, can help hide it from the police. It's like a wardrobe change, but for your vehicle. Pay 'N' Spray is the place to go for a quick paint job, while mod shops will be able to make more extensive changes to your car.
Overall, it seems like Rockstar has found a nice balance between the realities of car ownership and the escapist fantasy that the Grand Theft Auto series has always embodied. We'll just have to wait and see if "Car Mechanic Simulator 2027" will be adding heists.

articles.t: GTA 6 sur PC : CyberLeek promet l'émulation en une semaine
articles.chapeau: Le groupe CyberLeek affirme diffuser par torrent une build Xbox de GTA 6. L'exécutable manque, promis contre la hausse de sa cryptomonnaie.
articles.txt:
Le jour même de la sortie de Grand Theft Auto VI , le groupe CyberLeek a refait surface. Une mise à jour publiée sur son site le 19 novembre renvoie vers un fichier intitulé « XBOX BUILD 1.0.2.1 (NOV 2026) ». Le groupe affirme détenir la version complète du jeu de Rockstar Games , compilée en novembre 2026 pour Xbox Series X|S , et la distribuer par torrent. « C'est fait. Elle est diffusée par torrent. Maintenant » , annonce le message, relayé par Kotaku et Video Games Chronicle .
L'archive pèse 209 Go, un volume signalé sur les réseaux sociaux par Jose Coixao le soir même ( ndlr : son compte X n'existe plus à l'heure actuelle ). Il y manque un seul fichier, l'exécutable principal, sans lequel rien ne peut se lancer. CyberLeek le retient derrière un compte à rebours : « À zéro, l'exécutable est publié, sans condition » . Le groupe promet de le libérer plus tôt si son jeton $CYBERLEEK atteint une capitalisation de 15 millions de dollars. Le seuil était fixé à 30 millions en octobre, avant que le cours ne s'effondre. « C'était trop ambitieux. La moitié semble juste » , justifie désormais le site. Le groupe avait alors multiplié les fuites, jusqu'à des images dénudées de Lucia, l'une des deux héroïnes jouables.
Ni Kotaku ni VGC n'ont pu vérifier le contenu de l'archive. Les captures qui circulent semblent montrer les fichiers d'une build de développement, sans plus. Rockstar et Take-Two n'ont pas réagi à cette nouvelle fuite. L'éditeur a déjà lancé plusieurs assignations visant Discord pour identifier les membres du groupe, sans résultat visible à ce jour.
La promesse vise d'abord les joueurs PC, puisque le jeu n'est sorti que sur PS5 et Xbox Series . Le site l'assume sans détour : « C'est une version Xbox cette fois, pas une version PC. CL s'en moque. Cette communauté l'aura émulée en moins d'une semaine, bien au-delà de 30 images par seconde » . Il évoque aussi une build PS5 en solution de repli si la version Xbox ne donne rien, une option « probablement jamais nécessaire » . Aucune démonstration n'appuie ces affirmations. Une build Xbox ne se lance pas telle quelle sous Windows : il faut comprendre et contourner l'environnement de la console, et aucun émulateur Xbox Series fonctionnel n'existe aujourd'hui. Côté PlayStation, la scène s'active autour d' un premier dump de GTA 6 sur PS5 , mais l'émulation de la console reste balbutiante.
Le choix d'une version Xbox plutôt que PS5 intrigue, et le délai annoncé laisse sceptique. Dans la scène, l'idée qui domine est qu'un GTA VI jouable sur PC prendra des années plutôt que des jours, pour un jeu réputé plafonner à 30 images par seconde sur consoles. Les quelques jeux Xbox récents qui tournent sur PC, comme les Forza , le doivent à leur propre version Windows, pas à un émulateur.
CyberLeek se présente en défenseur des consommateurs. Il reproche à Rockstar une sortie sans disque, dont l'édition physique se limite à un code de téléchargement . Son message lance « pas de double paiement pour Take-Two et Rockstar » et rappelle avoir conseillé de ne pas précommander : « Voici l'une des raisons » . Depuis des mois, le groupe publie des extraits de gameplay authentiques. Il réserve aussi le vote dans ses sondages aux auteurs de dons en cryptomonnaie, et, selon Kotaku , il a déjà encaissé une partie des gains de son jeton.
Le groupe ne s'en cache pas. Dans un message intitulé « The End of the Road », publié en octobre et toujours visible sur son site, il reconnaît : « CL a vendu deux fois » . La première vente aurait déclenché une cascade, les autres détenteurs revendant à leur tour, et le groupe s'est vu reprocher l'effondrement du cours. Sa défense tient en deux phrases : « Le jeton a toujours été un don, jamais un investissement. Aucun rendement promis, ni sous-entendu » . Les accusations, elles, viendraient de « gens qui n'ont jamais ouvert la blockchain. Surtout des YouTubeurs » . Le seuil de 15 millions de dollars a de quoi faire sourire, et l'idée d'un collectif qui joue les justiciers surtout pour l'argent revient souvent dans les discussions. Une version sans DRM ne déplairait pourtant pas à tout le monde.
Après la fuite de la tracklist de l'album et celle de séquences de jeu, le lancement de GTA VI reste sous pression. Tant que rien n'est vérifié, la prudence s'impose : n'acheter aucun jeton, ne connecter aucun portefeuille de cryptomonnaies et ne lancer aucun exécutable d'origine inconnue. articles.t: GTA 6's Mandy Is Lexie Shoaibi: Actress Confirms Voice and Mocap Role for Viral Tenant - Shane the Gamer
articles.chapeau: Lexie Shoaibi has confirmed she plays Mandy, the flirty tenant from GTA 6's Pipework mission who took over social feeds within hours of the game's launch.
articles.txt:
You turn up to collect the rent. Instead you’re elbow-deep in a blocked sink while the tenant tells you you’re meant to be together. That’s Pipework, an early Jason mission in Grand Theft Auto VI, and the tenant at its centre now has a name and a face: Lexie Shoaibi confirmed in an Instagram post that she plays Mandy in Rockstar Games’ latest title.
Shoaibi said she provided both the voice and motion capture for Mandy, and LADbible reports the video went up on Thursday, 19 November. That’s launch day. Her line was simple: “I play Mandy,” followed by an invite for players to tell her if they’d found her in the game.
It isn’t just her word, either. According to ComicBook.com, Rockstar Games revealed who plays the character alongside the full cast on 19 November. Insider Gaming also points to the official GTA 6 cast list as naming Shoaibi.
That matters because the internet got there messily first. Insider Gaming notes that several people online have claimed that they are Mandy in GTA 6, but those claims are not the case. Now that both the cast list and the actress herself have confirmed it, that argument’s over.
The fan reaction has mostly been people jokingly picking Mandy over Jason’s actual partner:
Mandy’s screen time is short. GTABase describes her as one of Brian Heder’s tenants in the Leonida Keys, and she has a crush on Jason. She refuses to pay until he fixes her sink, and the mission becomes a plunger-and-wrench minigame while she keeps flirting.
If you’re hoping it goes somewhere, it doesn’t. Video Games Chronicle is blunt: Jason can’t romance Mandy, no matter how you approach the mission. PowerPyx’s walkthrough says the outcome is the same every time: Jason refuses her sexual advances, then she gets mad and tosses the cigar box out into the street.
There’s one small extra after the mission. Per VGC’s reporting, Jason gets a text message from Mandy saying she knows he wants her but can’t admit it. It’s flavour text. You can’t reply your way into a romance.
Here’s what makes the spike interesting. ComingSoon notes that Mandy’s popularity has emerged despite Rockstar not featuring her in any of the game’s trailers or promotional material. Years of trailer breakdowns, and the breakout character is a tenant with a clogged sink nobody had seen before.
LADbible collected some of the fan posts, including one that read “You can’t put Mandy in GTA VI and expect me to stay loyal to Lucia.” Vice reported that many players started searching whether it was possible “to cheat” on Lucia. The answer’s still no.
Our view: this is Rockstar doing what it always does. The marketing sells the leads, and then some one-scene weirdo steals the first weekend. GTA V had plenty of those. This time the meme machine just runs a lot faster.
Read also: GTA 6 Skips PC on November 19, but WoW: Forever and Warhammer Survivors Arrive This Month
Shoaibi’s a newcomer to games. ComicBook.com says this is the first video game Shoaibi has appeared in. Her screen work is a short list.
LADbible lists Paradise by the Dashboard Light (2016), The Good Fight (2017), Hollywood (2020) and Atom (2021), as well as voicing Dr. MedusaSaurus in the animated series Hamster & Gretel (2022–2023). That fits a familiar pattern. As ComicBook.com puts it, Rockstar Games often uses lesser-known acting talents, especially ones with no track record in video games.
It’s a casting approach that keeps Leonida from feeling like a celebrity cameo reel. It also means the people behind these characters can go from a handful of credits to the most-searched name in gaming overnight.
ComicBook.com floated the idea that her reception could change in the future, particularly with GTA Online content. That’s speculation. Rockstar hasn’t announced anything, and in the story as it stands, it appears players encounter Mandy only once.
If you ask us, a cameo in Online is the obvious move once the multiplayer side spins up. Rockstar has never been shy about bringing story favourites back. For now, Mandy lives in one Chapter 1 mission in Key Lento, plus one follow-up text, and you can replay it as often as you like.

CyberLeek Claims to Have Released 209GB GTA 6 Build, but Executable Is Missing - SSBCrack News
articles.chapeau: CyberLeek, the online persona of a group previously linked to leaks of Grand Theft Auto 6 gameplay, claims it has begun distributing a 209GB development build
articles.txt:
CyberLeek, the online persona of a group previously linked to leaks of Grand Theft Auto 6 gameplay, claims it has begun distributing a 209GB development build of the game. The group says the files represent a November 2026 build, potentially close to—or identical to—the version intended for release.
The claim could not be independently verified. Although the download’s advertised size was visible on CyberLeek’s site, the existence of the files themselves has not been confirmed. The build also appears to be missing its main executable, which would be needed to run the game. CyberLeek says it is withholding that file and may publish it later.
In a statement posted on its site, the group said it had the “full November 2026 build” and that it was being distributed by torrent, with the executable held “on a countdown.” CyberLeek says it will release that file ahead of schedule if its cryptocurrency token reaches a set value. The group’s previous leaks have also been associated with a crypto scheme, which was earlier estimated to have generated at least £200,000 for those behind it.
CyberLeek first threatened to release a complete, playable build in October. Its latest claims raise the possibility that the game could be made to run on PC before Rockstar announces an official PC version. However, that outcome remains uncertain: the build has not been verified, and the missing executable currently prevents it from being launched. Rumours have suggested a PC release could follow the console launch by several months, but Rockstar has not announced a PC release.
The group says it expects the Xbox build to be made to work and claims a community could have it running through emulation within a week. It also said it would seek a PlayStation 5 build as a fallback if the Xbox version proves unusable. These claims have not been independently confirmed.
CyberLeek has previously framed its actions as a campaign for “Gamers’ Rights,” citing opposition to the industry’s move toward digital-only games and the discontinuation of physical discs. Rockstar has described the earlier leaks as “heartbreaking,” saying they were not how the company intended players to see the game. Take-Two Interactive has also sought information about the leaker’s identity through a subpoena to Discord.

Cyberleek releases GTA 6 Xbox build, making playable PC port more realistic
articles.chapeau: Cyberleek has made another comeback, leaking a November GTA 6 Xbox build. The download lacks the vital executable file, with its release timing depending on a new cryptocurrency goal. Hackers are studying the files for a potential Series X emulator or decompilation build on PCs.
articles.txt:
Just when it seemed Cyberleek had disappeared for good, the notorious leaker has returned. Even though the GTA 6 release date has passed, the individual has followed through on past threats. A decrypted Xbox build is spreading through piracy networks, which could lead to a playable PC port . However, there is one major caveat with the 209 GB download.
The Cyberleek website now displays a message about the latest leak. While prior gameplay videos appeared to be from a PC-based development build , they elected to distribute GTA 6 Xbox files. Allegedly, this version is from November 2026, and images of a file structure exposing assets have emerged. Regardless, it may have limited use without the missing executable file.
Once again, Cyberleek hopes to raise cryptocurrency funds before releasing the critical file. Offering a playable build as the reward, they previously set a $30 million market capitalization goal for a meme coin. That October initiative failed, but hitting the $15 million mark will supposedly unlock the .exe.
Notably, a timer is also counting down from under 4 days. Once it expires, Rockstar ’s tormentor promises to circulate the executable on piracy sites anyway.
It's unclear how soon the GTA 6 Xbox files may result in a bootable game for PC users. Cyberleek believes hackers will find a way to emulate the console version for Windows within a week. As criticism of the 30 fps performance target continues, capable hardware could produce higher frame rates.
Unfortunately for pirates, no working Series X emulator currently exists. The hardware found in the Microsoft console and many PCs is similar, with CPUs sharing x86-64 architecture. Still, among other challenges, the Series X runs a custom OS that would need to be adapted for a Windows environment.
Another possibility is a decompilation project targeting the leaked GTA 6 Xbox files. Developers would analyze, modify, and reconstruct the code into a version that can boot on PCs.
Cyberleek also claims to possess a PS5 build as a fallback option. Besides accumulating cryptocurrency, the objective is to prevent console and PC ports from doubling Take-Two and Rockstar's profits.

GTA VI Leaker Releases 209 GB Xbox Build Without Main Executable
articles.chapeau: A GTA VI leaker has released a claimed 209 GB Xbox build without its executable, with the missing file tied to a countdown and cryptocurrency target.
articles.txt:
Cyberleek, the group behind earlier GTA VI leaks, has released what they claim is a complete November 2026 Xbox build of Grand Theft Auto VI, minus the main executable needed to run the game. The GTA VI Xbox build leak surfaced on November 19, the same day Rockstar Games’ latest open-world title launched on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.
The torrent is approximately 209 GB and contains what appear to be the game’s data and pack folders, RPF archives, and Xbox-specific configuration files.
According to announcements published on Cyberleek’s website, the missing executable will be released once a countdown expires. The leaker is also offering to release it earlier if a cryptocurrency token named CYBERLEEK reaches a market capitalization of $15 million. That target was previously set at $30 million before being reduced.
Cyberleek has also discussed the possibility of pursuing a PlayStation 5 build if the leaked Xbox files cannot be made to work. The leaker claimed that the community could emulate the Xbox version within a week, although there is currently no evidence that such an effort will succeed.
The GTA VI Xbox build leak has attracted attention on Reddit’s r/Piracy community, where several users claim to have examined the files. One commenter said they discovered 145 mission records inside a common.rpf archive, including references to the game’s protagonists, Lucia and Jason.
Cyberleek previously attracted scrutiny from Take-Two Interactive after releasing gameplay footage, map information, and a 24-minute cutscene earlier this fall. Those earlier leaks were also connected to the same cryptocurrency token.
The authenticity of the newly released Xbox files remains unconfirmed, and the missing executable has not been made publicly available.

articles.t: Infamous GTA 6 leaker CyberLeek is back, and this time the group claims to have leaked a full development build of the game
articles.chapeau: The latest CyberLeek upload is titled: "XBOX BUILD 1.0.2.1 (NOV 2026)" and it's a big one.
articles.txt:
CyberLeek, the persona of a hacker group that was responsible for leaking GTA 6 gameplay before the game launched, has reappeared today, claiming to have released a development build of the final version of the game on its site. This new leak appears to be making good on a threat posted back in October, where the group stated its intent to release a full, playable build of the game .
Various social media accounts have visited the site and noted the size of the download offered by CyberLeek is, indeed 209GB. Eurogamer has seen the site and can confirm this is what the group has claimed, however I have been unable to verify the existence of any actual files. On the site, CyberLeek claims this build is from November 2026 - meaning it is very close to (if not the actual) release build. The 'executable file appears to be missing from the build, however, meaning you cannot actually - yet - get it up and running. CyberLeek is threatening to release this file at a later date, however.
"It is done," a statement from CyberLeek reads. "[Cyberleek] holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto 6, and it is going out by torrent. Now. Every file except one. The main executable is held on a countdown." CyberLeek says the executable will be released earlier than planned if its crypto token reaches a predetermined value. Many of the leaks to date have been related to a CyberLeek crypto scheme. Previously, it was estimated that the group cashed out at least £200,000.
What does all this mean? There's a very realistic chance that the game could be up and running on PC soon - undercutting Rockstar's unannounced PC release by a matter of months , if current rumours are to be believed. "This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps," the statement continues. "[CyberLeek] told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons.
"If the Xbox build cannot be made to work and support holds, [CyberLeek] will work to get a PS5 build - a fallback, most likely never required. Either way: the Xbox build is going out. No double dipping for Take-Two/Rockstar." It seems these are not empty threats.
CyberLeek has been a thorn in Rockstar's side for a while now. The group initially claimed it took this action in the name of "Gamers' Rights", supposedly fighting for consumers in relation to the controversial discontinuation of game-discs and the digital-only future being pursued by game publishers. Rockstar has previously issued statements regarding the leaker , noting that the leaks are "heartbreaking" and that "this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time". Take-Two tried to subpoena Discord for information pertaining to the leaker's identity.

articles.chapeau: CyberLeek claims to have shared a 209 GB Xbox build of GTA 6 on launch day. The leaker says the missing executable will follow when a countdown ends.
articles.txt:
CyberLeek has returned, claiming to leak a 209GB GTA 6 Xbox build, but withheld the executable. They’re demanding crypto funding, so skepticism—and avoiding payment—is strongly advised.
On October 14, CyberLeek signed off with a three-part statement titled The End of the Road. “The leeks stop here. For now.” Turns out “for now” meant 36 days. It’s GTA 6 launch day and CyberLeek is back, claiming to have released a November Xbox build of the game via torrent. The download reportedly weighs in at 209 GB. The one file CyberLeek says they’ve kept to themselves is the executable you’d need to actually run the thing.
Aside from the executable, the download seems real and does seem to be the game files, at least according to people who have already jumped on and checked it all out. Obviously, I won’t be linking to the files here.
According to a statement attributed to CyberLeek and reproduced on Reddit, the executable will be released when a countdown hits zero. That countdown will end on November. There is, of course, a way to speed that up, because of course there is. If the leaker’s cryptocurrency reaches a $15 million market cap, they say they’ll release the file immediately. “30 million was too ambitious; half that seems fair,” reads the statement.
This seems utterly stupid. Why pay a bunch of money to this CyberLeek entity if they are already saying they’ll give you the missing file in 4 days anyway?
Back in October, CyberLeek promised to release the entire game if the coin hit that massive $30 million target. When the coin fell woefully short, the leaker said uploading more than 200 GB anonymously was too risky without the money to fund their “secret project”.
What’s changed is that there’s now a package people can inspect. If those 209 GB check out, which they seem to, then I’d be surprised if CyberLeek had somehow got hold of everything except the executable. Whether they’ll ever part with it is another question.
Which brings me to the choice of platform. The earlier footage was widely thought to show the game running on PC. If CyberLeek had a working PC build back then, what happened to that one? Why are we wow we’re being offered Xbox files with the executable held back? CyberLeek reckons somebody else will have the game emulated for PC inside a week, also begging the queston of why not release the PC build you seemingly already had? In the very same statement, they say they’ll try to get a PS5 build if the Xbox one doesn’t work and support holds.
Could somebody eventually get these files running on PC? I’m well outside my area of expertise on that one. The recompilation projects seen for older Xbox games typically start with the compiled game code or the source code , which is exactly why that missing executable matters. These files might give somebody a head start, but I’ve yet to see anyone demonstrate a PC version running from this download. Of course, it’s only been like five minutes, so it’s hardly a surprise nothing has popped up yet.
The bit I keep coming back to, though, is November. CyberLeek was already showing off 25 minutes of GTA 6 in early October, teasing that they already had a full build at that point. If “the full November 2026 build” means a newer version than the one in that footage, how did they get their hands on it this close to launch? Did they still have a source inside Rockstar feeding them newer builds? Or did they only get access to a complete copy recently, after spending October promising they could release one? Was the earlier footage actually from a much smaller version of the game?
There’s a simpler possibility, too. With GTA 6 now on sale, these could be files from the retail Xbox release. A build number we could put alongside the retail one would tell us a hell of a lot more about where those 209 GB came from.
The other piece of timing is also interesting: the game is out now. CyberLeek waited to return and actually release files until the game launched. That doesn’t inspire confidence in some of his earlier build claims.
His target now is realistically PC gamers since they are being forced to sit and watch their console brethren enjoy the game, with zero announced launch date for the PC build. Again, though, questions must be asked: if PC gamers are the ones most eager to actually get the game, why release an Xbox build? Was it always an Xbox build? Hmm.
There’s too much strangness. None of this makes real sense, to me.

GTA 6’s Best-Kept Secret Is the Most Important Part of the Game
articles.chapeau: The prologue of GTA 6 starts with a shock
articles.txt:
Considering how much of Grand Theft Auto 6 leaked before its launch, you’d think that Rockstar’s latest wouldn’t have anything left to hide. I mean, we’ve really seen it all. But as players immediately discovered when starting their save file, Rockstar (kind of) managed to keep one secret — and it was a huge one.
[Ed. note: This article contains spoilers for the prologue of GTA 6. ]
GTA 6 kicks off with a short prologue chapter that sets a few things in motion . First, we get to see the moment Jason and Lucia met , as they both got crossed trying to jack the same car. A rom-com montage ensues, but things take a turn fast. We fast-forward to Lucia sitting in a restaurant as she prepares to pull off a robbery across the street. After nervously stalling , she works up the courage to stick the place up. Unfortunately, it doesn’t go well. The cops quickly intervene and arrest her.
The twist comes as she’s being put into the back of a cop car. A panicked Lucia begs the cops to take her back to the restaurant where she was holed up before the robbery, because she left something there. The cops discover something that the camera was carefully hiding earlier in the sequence: Lucia’s infant son, Tommy, who she left unattended.
As we soon learn, Tommy is Jason and Lucia’s son. Tommy now lives with a separate guardian after getting taken from Lucia’s custody; Jason and Lucia only get to see him through occasional photos that get texted to them. It turns out that Jason and Lucia’s whole motivation for making cash in GTA 6 is to fund a family savings account in hopes that they can reunite with their son and give him a normal life.
Image: Rockstar Games via Polygon It’s a shocking revelation that Rockstar desperately wanted to keep hidden as long as possible. No pre-release trailers for the game so much as teased that there was a kid in the picture. When I spoke to Rockstar North co-head Rob Nelson just ahead of the game’s launch, he seemed relieved that the detail had mostly gone unspoiled, despite a cavalcade of leaks. (It actually did leak about a year ago, but it faded into a forgotten rumor in a sea of them by the time GTA 6 actually launched.) For Nelson, that initial shock is an important part of an experience that’s designed to challenge what you think you know about its antiheroes at every turn.
With Tommy comes a mess of complicated character dynamics and anxieties that you’ll see throughout GTA 6 ’s story. While Lucia seems like an impulsive loudmouth who doesn’t have a care in the world, it becomes increasingly clear that she’s harboring serious insecurity after having Tommy taken from her. She quietly worries that she doesn’t deserve to be a parent after leaving her kid to go pull off a stick-up. While Jason wasn’t part of that, he holds the same fear that someone like him isn’t responsible enough to be a father. Those feelings bleed out whenever the two receive a text with a photo of Tommy and are reminded of the kid who is growing up somewhere without them.
Tommy also adds some welcome tension into Jason and Lucia’s love story, considering that the romance can be largely free of friction otherwise (depending on how you engage with the romance system). At one point, the two broke into a spontaneous conversation about their family. Jason noted that Lucia’s mother doesn’t seem to like him very much, which prompted Lucia to reveal that she lied to her mom and told her that Jason didn’t want to be involved in Tommy’s life. Though that isn’t exactly true given that Jason didn’t know his son existed, Lucia then recalled a conversation where Jason told her he didn’t want to have kids. That exchange gives us context that explains why Lucia didn’t tell Jason about Tommy upfront. For Nelson, those little details help build a nuanced story of two reluctant parents trying to figure out how to adapt to an unexpected responsibility.

And while stories about parenting might feel a little played out in a world where the “ dad game ” has become a tired trope, it’s refreshing to have one that has so much compassion for everyone involved. It’s sympathetic to Lucia’s circumstances, making a point in a flashback to show her struggling to live as a single mother in a world that is hostile to her specific needs. articles.txt:
From the sun-soaked synth-pop of Vice City to surfing a sea of radio stations, music has always been an essential part of Rockstar Games' gritty, open-world franchise. And with Grand Theft Auto VI taking players back to Vice City, the sprawling soundtrack is shaping up to be just as ambitious as the game itself.
Rockstar has already revealed a 34-track album featuring artists like Travis Scott, Cardi B, and PinkPantheress, along with an original score composed by the French electronic duo Justice. Meanwhile, the game's fictional radio stations are bringing some familiar voices to the airwaves, including Robyn, Bad Bunny, and Lana Del Rey.
And that's just what we know so far. Ahead of GTA 6 's Nov. 19 release , we're keeping track of every confirmed song, artist, radio station, and celebrity DJ coming to Leonida. Consider this your unofficial guide to the sounds of Vice City.
Rockstar has announced Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album , a 34-track collection of original music arriving Nov. 19, the same day as the game.
The album features an eclectic mix of artists and genres , from hip-hop heavyweights Travis Scott and Cardi B to country star Morgan Wallen and Puerto Rican singer Rauw Alejandro. There's even a collaboration between CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso, PinkPantheress, Fred again.., and French producer Etienne de Crécy. And somehow, someway, Morgan Wallen's single is the most-streamed track from the soundtrack on Spotify, with more than 25 million streams. Yung Lean, fight back!
"Sexy Magic" — CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso, PinkPantheress, Fred again.. & Étienne de Crécy

The French electronic duo Justice, consisting of Gaspard Augé and Xavier de Rosnay, is responsible for the original score of Grand Theft Auto VI .
Rockstar confirmed the news on Oct. 15 alongside the game's launch trailer , which features the debut of Justice's new single, "Flower in a Hurricane," featuring Tame Impala, SZA, and Australian psychedelic rock band King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard.
It's a fitting collaboration for a game returning to Vice City, a fictional playground known for its vibrant nightlife and electronic music. Justice's signature blend of distorted synths, disco, and dance music feels particularly suited to Rockstar's radiant criminal underworld.
The duo previously collaborated with Tame Impala on "Neverender" from their 2024 album Hyperdrama . The song won Best Dance/Electronic Recording at the 2025 Grammys.
Rockstar has also confirmed that an official score album is on the way, although additional details, including its release date and tracklist, have yet to be announced.
The fictional radio stations are one of Grand Theft Auto 's most beloved features, and GTA 6 is bringing some major star power to the airwaves.

Metal fans aren't being left out. Slayer's Kerry King and Tom Araya host The Chamber , a station dedicated to heavy metal.

articles.txt:
Grand Theft Auto 6, le jeu le plus attendu de l’année, voire de la décennie, est sorti à midi heure française en Nouvelle-Zélande. Donnant aux joueurs les plus impatients les premières images.
Depuis des semaines, le monde du jeu vidéo n’attend que ça : ça y est, Grand Theft Auto (GTA) 6 est enfin disponible, treize ans après le cinquième volet . Et les premiers chanceux à pouvoir y jouer sont les Néo-Zélandais, grâce au décalage horaire. Rockstar Games, l’éditeur du jeu, a en effet choisi de sortir son produit phare le jeudi 19 novembre à minuit heure locale de chaque pays. En France donc, les premières images et diffusions en direct sont accessibles depuis ce mercredi midi.
Une attente interminable et enfin les premières images, y compris venant de streamers français étant parvenus à mettre leur console à l’heure néo-zélandaise . Un premier chargement long, très long, laissant craindre à un bug. Puis des paramètres à configurer, reculant encore l’arrivée à Vice City, lieu où se déroule le jeu.
🚨BREAKING: GTA 6 Game intro officially released pic.twitter.com/UsX6ndby4n
D’entrée, le ton est donné : une première cinématique. Une voiture en train d’être volée et les deux protagonistes : Lucia et Jason. La police qui intervient, un premier coup de poing et des forces de l’ordre tabassées. Le tout avec une musique immersive, mais bloquée chez certains streamers pour des raisons de droits d’auteur. Bienvenue dans GTA 6. La scène suivante montre les deux protagonistes chez eux… en pleine embrouille.
Après de nombreux crédits, une nouvelle cinématique transporte le joueur dans la vie de Lucia, neuf mois avant les premières scènes. Puis un nouveau flash-back. Lucia est cette fois en prison, tenue orange typique des détenus américains sur le dos.
Officially GTA 6 GAMEPLAY ( Intro Prison Scene #GTA6 ) pic.twitter.com/4R7FMkitnI
C’est là que le jeu commence vraiment. Lucia est contrôlable dans un monde ouvert, typique des GTA aux graphiques qui semblent soignés malgré les 30 images par seconde. Fidèle aux attentes sur ce point.
L’ellipse narrative prend fin, retour dans un bar avec Lucia. Quelques secondes après, on la retrouve pistolet à la main en plein braquage d’un point de retrait d’argent. Le joueur reprend la main en pleine fuite, coursée par la police. La première séquence avec Jason survient pour sa part sur un bateau, suivie d’une première mission où le joueur est amené (très) largement à utiliser son arme à feu et à esquiver les balles.
HAHAHA il a réussi à rater le tuto de GTA 6 😭 pic.twitter.com/RelSWLyi5z
Sans grande surprise, les premiers instants de ce nouvel opus transportent le joueur directement dans ce qu’il attendait : l’intrigue, le cadre, les armes… En moins d’une heure, il aura contrôlé deux personnages, une voiture, un bateau et… un hydravion avec lequel il est possible de s’amuser à faire des loopings ou de se crasher. Bref un monde où presque tout est permis dès les débuts.
Dès 11h45 heure française, mois d’une demi-heure donc avant le début des premières diffusions en direct, plus de 650 000 spectateurs de tous les pays attendaient déjà sur la plate-forme Twitch . Et le chiffre n’a cessé de monter pour dépasser le million à midi et les 2,5 millions à 12h40.
« Il y a de fortes chances que Twitch vive son plus grand record d’audience jamais enregistré », glissait au Parisien début novembre Dan Clancy, son PDG. D’après le cabinet spécialisé Sensor Tower, le jeu a été précommandé à plus de quinze millions d’exemplaires partout dans le monde.

articles.t: Arion Kurtaj a plaidé coupable dans l’affaire de la fuite de GTA VI
GTA VI : la carte de Leonida a fuité et elle est immense
articles.chapeau: Les cartes de GTA VI ont fuité, et la fuite semble crédible : cinq comtés, des marais, une Floride entière à explorer. De quoi faire saliver les joueurs avant même d’avoir touché la manette.
articles.txt:
Les cartes de GTA VI ont fuité, et la fuite semble crédible : cinq comtés, des marais, une Floride entière à explorer. De quoi faire saliver les joueurs avant même d’avoir touché la manette.
À quelques heures de la sortie de GTA VI , deux cartes de Leonida attirent l’attention des joueurs sur les réseaux sociaux. L’une est une carte géographique colorée avec routes, îles et cours d’eau, comme on pourrait en trouver sur Google Maps ou Apple Plans. L’autre est une carte illustrée avec cinq comtés. Leur origine exacte n’est pas établie. Mais elles recoupent ce qu’on sait du poster fourni avec la Vice City Collection.
Publiées par le compte ViceWire | Rockstar News, ces deux cartes seraient en réalité présentes dans la Vice City Collection, cette “édition collector” du jeu vendue 399 € et pourtant dépourvue du jeu. Le coffret contient notamment une figurine de Macca the Gator, des lunettes Oakley Frogskins, une cuillère à cocktail, mais aussi un poster recto-verso, comprenant selon toute vraisemblance la carte du jeu.
🚨 TWO DIFFERENT #GTAVI LEONIDA MAPS HAVE NOW BEEN REVEALED! 🗺️🌴🔥
We're finally getting a detailed look at TWO map designs from the GTA VI Vice City Collection!
🗺️ LEFT: A colourful geographical map showing Leonida's roads, highways, islands, cities and surrounding waterways.… pic.twitter.com/MZBeaDmzP7
— ViceWire | Rockstar News 🌴 (@ViceWireGTAVI) November 13, 2026
Et si cette fuite était avérée, on aurait tout bonnement affaire à la plus grande carte jamais proposée dans un jeu Grand Theft Auto . La carte de la fuite laisse notamment entrevoir les cinq comtés qui composeront l’état de Leonida. Lummox se situe au nord, Kelly à l’ouest, Leonard à l’est, Vice-Dale autour de Vice City et Mariana, l’équivalent des Everglades, au sud de la carte, dans les zones humides.
Lorsque l’on compare ces deux cartes avec l’image officielle fournie par Rockstar pour illustrer le verso du poster, la fuite devient tout de suite plus crédible. On reconnaît le lettrage de Leonida sur la gauche et notamment le soleil, en haut à gauche de la carte. En revanche, les Leonida Keys n’apparaissent pas sur la carte qui a fuité. La carte est bien entendue inspirée de la Floride, on y retrouverait notamment des péages, un grand aéroport au sud-ouest de Vice City et donc cette chaîne d’îles au sud, semblables aux Keys de Floride.
Cette fuite révèle énormément de choses sur cette map qu’il nous tarde tant de découvrir. On apprend ainsi que les zones rurales s’étendent du nord à l’ouest, et que les marais sont présents au sud de la carte. Selon de nombreuses sources, la carte de Leonida serait près de deux fois plus grande que celle de GTA V , passant de 81 km² pour l’épisode de 2013 à près de 150 km² de terrain explorable dans GTA VI.
Pour rappel, une des traditions de Rockstar était d’inclure une carte papier dans la boîte de chaque exemplaire du jeu vendu. Celui-ci étant disponible depuis le 12 novembre dernier, Rockstar a probablement voulu éviter les spoils en n’incluant pas cette fameuse carte dans l’édition “physique”. Une carte téléchargeable gratuitement sera toutefois mise à disposition des joueurs au lancement du jeu, ou peu de temps après, et une version physique vendue sur le site.

articles.t: Le hacker de GTA 6 plaide coupable : il a bien piraté Rockstar Games en 2022
articles.chapeau: Arion Kurtaj, le Britannique à l’origine de la fuite massive de Grand Theft Auto VI en 2022, a plaidé coupable le 16 novembre 2026 devant la justice britannique. Le tout à quelques jours de la sortie du jeu le plus attendu de tous les temps.
articles.txt:
Arion Kurtaj, le Britannique à l’origine de la fuite massive de Grand Theft Auto VI en 2022, a plaidé coupable le 16 novembre 2026 devant la justice britannique. Le tout à quelques jours de la sortie du jeu le plus attendu de tous les temps.
Le 18 septembre 2022, Rockstar Games était victime de l’une des fuites les plus importantes de l’histoire du jeu vidéo . Arion Kurtaj, alors âgé de 17 ans , a récupéré 90 séquences de gameplay . Arrêté et condamné depuis, il est repassé devant la justice pénale et pour la première fois, il a reconnu les faits.
Fin 2022, Arion Kurtaj, alors âgé de 17 ans, est impliqué dans les intrusions du groupe Lapsus$ contre Nvidia, BT/EE, Revolut . Il est arrêté et placé en détention provisoire , puis libéré sous caution dans l’attente de son procès. Une période durant laquelle il est hébergé dans un hôtel sous protection policière, puisque menacé par d’autres pirates à propos de bitcoins volés.
Privé d’ordinateur, Arion Kurtaj a utilisé un Amazon Fire Stick à l’arrière de la télévision de sa chambre, un clavier et une souris et a piraté Rockstar Games. Avec ce hack, il a récupéré 90 séquences de gameplay de GTA VI , accède au canal de communication interne de l’entreprise et menace de publier le code s’il n’est pas contacté. Faute de réponse, le jeune homme a diffusé toutes les vidéos et le code source sur un forum.
Sauf qu’il est repéré et devra rendre des comptes. En 2023 lors de son procès, les médecins ont estimé que la gravité de son autisme rendait Arion Kurtaj inapte à être jugé dans un procès pénal ordinaire. En décembre de la même année, le jury a conclu qu’Arion Kurtaj a bien commis ces actes et a prononcé une ordonnance d’hospitalisation sécurisée à durée indéterminée. Pour lui, le jeune hacker représentait toujours un danger ; il pourrait retomber dans le cybercrime.
Mais voilà, fin 2025, une évaluation médicale de routine l’a déclaré apte à être jugé. Une décision qui a entraîné son transfert d’un hôpital sécurisé vers une prison classique en janvier dernier. Ce changement de statut médical a permis l’ouverture d’ une procédure pénale classique devant la Woolwich Crown Court. Le 16 novembre, Arion Kurtaj a enfin plaidé coupable pour l’ensemble des chefs d’accusation, dont le piratage de Rockstar Games, en plus des attaques contre Uber, BT/EE et Revolut.
Désormais âgé de 21 ans, le hacker recevra sa sentence le 23 novembre prochain selon plusieurs médias. Le tribunal devra déterminer la peine appropriée ; les préjudices causés s’élèveraient à 10 millions de livres sterling. À noter qu’Arion Kurtaj a commis des violences physiques en détention et avait réussi à s’y procurer un téléphone portable, ce qui est interdit.
Ce nouveau procès s’est ouvert en marge de la sortie de GTA VI , le jeu vidéo le plus attendu de tous les temps qu’Arion Kurtaj avait fait fuiter en 2022. Face à l’ampleur de ce piratage et des séquences du jeu, Rockstar Games avait dû confirmer l’authenticité de ces extraits, tout en précisant que le jeu était encore en développement . L’éditeur ne prévoyait pas du tout de parler de GTA VI aussi tôt : la première bande-annonce n’est arrivée que le 5 décembre 2023, plus d’un an après la fuite.
L’entreprise a estimé le coût de cette attaque à environ 5 millions de dollars, ce qui comprend notamment des milliers d’heures de travail pour ses équipes. En effet, il a fallu analyser l’ampleur de la compromission, sécuriser les systèmes et surtout gérer les conséquences de la publication de ces extraits du jeu. Un traumatisme pour les développeurs du jeu, mais aussi pour les fans : beaucoup auraient préféré que ce soit le studio qui montre en premier le jeu, pour respecter son travail. Une blessure qui va s’atténuer avec l’excitation de la sortie du jeu ce jeudi 19 novembre , 13 ans après l’arrivée d’un certain GTA V .

articles.t: Le hacker du leak GTA 6 plaide coupable à trois jours de la sortie
GTA 6 : le hacker derrière la fuite de 2022 plaide coupable, trois jours avant la sortie du jeu
articles.chapeau: À seulement trois jours de la sortie de GTA 6, le pirate à l'origine de la fuite massive de 2022, a plaidé coupable devant la justice britannique.
articles.txt:
À seulement trois jours de la sortie de GTA 6, le pirate à l’origine de la fuite massive de 2022, a plaidé coupable devant la justice britannique.
C’est un retour de bâton auquel on ne s’attendait plus à quelques jours du lancement le plus attendu de l’année. Arion Kurtaj, aujourd’hui âgé de 21 ans, a plaidé coupable ce 16 novembre 2026 devant le tribunal de Woolwich, à Londres, pour un méfait connu de toute la sphère vidéoludique. Il reconnaît être à l’origine du piratage de Rockstar Games en septembre 2022, qui avait permis la diffusion massive d’images de développement de Grand Theft Auto 6 . Il sera condamné le 23 novembre prochain, soit quatre jours après la sortie du jeu, prévue le 19 novembre.
À l’époque, Kurtaj n’avait que 17 ans et faisait partie du groupe de cybercriminels Lapsus$. L’intrusion avait provoqué un séisme dans l’industrie car, alors que Rockstar n’avait encore dévoilé aucune bande-annonce officielle, près de 90 vidéos du jeu en développement avaient été publiées sur internet. Au total, ces séquences représentaient presque une heure de gameplay, révélant de nombreux éléments que le studio a gardé secrets pendant plus de deux ans ensuite. La fuite était d’une ampleur jamais vue et avait forcé Rockstar à réagir publiquement.
L’histoire de cette intrusion est presque aussi improbable que son résultat était impressionnant. Kurtaj se trouvait à l’époque dans une chambre d’hôtel, où il avait été placé sous protection policière après avoir reçu des menaces de la part d’autres pirates informatiques. Son ordinateur ayant été confisqué, il aurait utilisé un téléphone portable, le réseau Wi-Fi de la télévision de sa chambre et une clé Amazon Fire TV Stick pour accéder aux systèmes de Rockstar. Il a ensuite récupéré les vidéos avant de les diffuser sous le pseudonyme TeaPotUberHacker.
Le pirate ne s’était pas arrêté à la publication des images puisqu’il avait également menacé de divulguer le code source de GTA 6 si Rockstar ne prenait pas contact avec lui. Le studio avait alors dû gérer une crise majeure, avec des conséquences financières et opérationnelles importantes. Selon les éléments rapportés par la BBC, Rockstar estimait le coût de la remise en état de ses systèmes à environ 5 millions de dollars, auxquels s’ajoutaient des milliers d’heures de travail mobilisées par ses équipes.
L’affaire a vite dépassé largement le cadre du jeu vidéo. Le hacker a également reconnu plusieurs autres attaques informatiques menées avec Lapsus$, notamment contre l’opérateur BT/EE, la plateforme financière Revolut et Uber. Cette dernière intrusion avait notamment entraîné le vol de données sensibles et la suppression de comptes et d’informations internes. Le parquet britannique évoque des dommages de plusieurs millions de dollars pour les entreprises ciblées.
Le parcours judiciaire du jeune homme est lui aussi particulier. En 2023, alors qu’il avait été jugé inapte à participer à un procès classique en raison de son autisme, un jury avait été chargé de déterminer s’il avait bien commis les actes reprochés, sans se prononcer sur son intention criminelle. Il avait ensuite été placé dans un établissement hospitalier sécurisé pour une durée indéterminée. Une évaluation ultérieure l’a finalement déclaré apte à comparaître, avant son transfert en prison en janvier 2026. Cette fois, le procès n’aura donc pas lieu car Kurtaj a plaidé coupable à l’ensemble des infractions retenues contre lui.

articles.t: Le pirate à l’origine de la fuite de GTA VI en 2022 plaide coupable devant un tribunal londonien
articles.chapeau: Sacré timing
articles.txt:
Arion Kurtaj, qui a diffusé en 2022 des images de développement de Grand Theft Auto VI après avoir piraté les serveurs de Rockstar, a plaidé coupable quatre ans plus tard. Selon la BBC , l’homme (qui avait 17 ans à l’époque, 21 aujourd'hui), a reconnu les faits lundi de cette semaine devant la Woolwich Crown Court, à Londres. Il a donc admis à la fois le piratage de Rockstar et plusieurs autres délits informatiques commis au sein du groupe Lapsus$.
Selon Kotaku , Kurtaj était sous caution pour d’autres faits lorsqu’il s’est introduit dans les serveurs de Rockstar, depuis une chambre d’hôtel où il se trouvait sous protection policière, avec une clé de streaming Amazon Fire Stick (on fait avec les moyens du bord). Il avait ensuite menacé l’entreprise sur son Slack, lui demandant de négocier avec lui via Telegram. Il avait plaidé non coupable en 2022, et Rockstar a refusé de négocier. Pour rappel, le jeune homme avait d’abord été jugé inapte à subir un procès, des professionnels de santé l’estimant dans l’incapacité d’y faire face, ce qui avait conduit à une décision d’enfermement dans un établissement hospitalier. Puis, en janvier 2026, révision de la décision : il a finalement été reconnu apte à être jugé, puis a plaidé coupable. Sa condamnation sera déterminée ultérieurement.
Bien entendu, ce n'est pas la seule affaire de fuite concernant GTA 6 : il n'aura échappé à personne que Cyberleek, responsable de nombreuses fuites du jeu au cours de l'été , est toujours en activité : il a même partagé de nouvelles images du jeu il y a quelques semaines seulement. Néanmoins, la machine marketing de GTA 6 est désormais bien trop imposante pour se faire voler la vedette, et le pirate n'a finalement jamais sorti son build du jeu (qu'il a pourtant menacé de libérer sur le net). Reste maintenant à voir si Rockstar, Take-Two et leurs avocats parviendront à retrouver le responsable de ces actions, pour lui réserver un sort similaire à celui d'Arion Kurtaj.
GTA 6 sera disponible dès le 19 novembre sur PS5 et Xbox Series X/S.

articles.chapeau: Arion Kurtaj a plaidé coupable devant la justice londonienne pour le piratage de Rockstar Games et la fuite de Grand Theft Auto VI survenue en 2022.
articles.txt:
Lire sur mobile Arion Kurtaj a plaidé coupable devant la justice londonienne pour le piratage de Rockstar Games et la fuite de Grand Theft Auto VI survenue en 2022. L'affaire avait fait grand bruit à l'automne 2022, lorsqu' une séquence de vidéos confidentielles de GTA 6 avait fuité . Aujourd'hui âgé de 21 ans, le Britannique Arion Kurtaj a plaidé coupable devant une cour de justice à Londres.
Membre du collectif Lapsus$, le jeune homme répond désormais de multiples chefs d'accusation pour fraude et accès non autorisé.
L'intrusion contre le studio à l'origine de Grand Theft Auto VI relève d'un scénario rocambolesque. Alors qu'il se trouvait en liberté conditionnelle dans un hôtel sous protection policière, l'adolescent a détourné une clé Amazon Fire TV reliée au téléviseur de sa chambre. Il a ensuite été en mesure de déjouer les sécurités internes de l'éditeur américain.
Son offensive a permis de dérober des vidéos de développement représentant une heure de gameplay inédit de la superproduction vidéoludique très attendue. L'attaquant a ultérieurement exigé une rançon sur la messagerie interne Slack en menaçant de divulguer le code source du projet.
Selon les déclarations de Rockstar Games, cette compromission a engendré plus de 5 millions de dollars de pertes directes et des milliers d'heures de travail.
La trajectoire pénale du jeune hacker a longtemps semblé bloquée par son état de santé mentale et son autisme sévère . Jugé initialement inapte à comparaître lors d'une première audience en 2023, il avait été placé sous un ordre d'hospitalisation sécurisée à durée indéterminée. Les médecins devaient alors évaluer régulièrement son état avant toute éventuelle remise en liberté.
Une réévaluation médicale routinière menée en janvier a conclu qu'il était apte à répondre de ses actes devant un tribunal classique. Transféré en détention ordinaire, l'accusé n'a pas tardé à récidiver en se procurant illicitement un téléphone portable pour narguer les autorités sur Snapchat.
Ces provocations répétées et plusieurs agressions contre le personnel soignant ont scellé son renvoi définitif devant la barre.
Les agissements du hacker ne se limitaient pas aux jeux vidéo et visaient des multinationales technologiques comme Uber, Revolut ou l'opérateur BT/EE. À travers des techniques d'ingénierie sociale et d'échange de cartes SIM, la bande organisée a détourné d'importantes sommes.
" Le prévenu faisait partie d'un groupe de pirates informatiques responsable d'attaques ayant engendré des pertes se chiffrant en millions de dollars ", a déclaré le procureur Robert Hutchinson .
" Ses agissements étaient prémédités . Même après avoir été inculpé pour des infractions graves, il a continué à prendre des organisations pour cible, faisant preuve d'un mépris constant tant pour les préjudices qu'il causait que pour la loi. " La peine prononcée contre Arion Kurtaj devrait être connue d'ici quelques jours.
